description: The relay's links' frames (docs/m4-design.md section 3). Long values are written compactly: `text`, `bytes`, `frame.message` and `frame.bytes` are each either the value itself (text, or hex) or an array of pieces to join in order, each piece either the value's text itself or {"repeat": text, "times": n}, that text written n times (n from 1 to 16,777,216); for hex fields every piece is hex and the joined text is the bytes' hex. Some frames carry an h of the right form that opens to nothing (1, the key id, a dot and 1,744 A's), since only the form is the frames' to check. `text`: one WebSocket text message travelling as `schema` names (hubToRelay and relayToHub on /v1/hub; relayToPush and pushToRelay on /v1/relay), which the receiver must accept as a frame (`accept` true) or refuse (false), refusing closes the link with 4400. A text frame is one JSON object whose `t` names it, with exactly the fields of section 3's tables (packages/protocol/src/relay/frames.ts) and no others, and at most 131,072 bytes of UTF-8, checked before parsing: a frame over it is refused even when its fields are valid, and a sender splits such a frame (the relay's push items) into several. `binary`: one WebSocket binary message: byte 0 the kind, then a u32 little-endian, then the payload. Kind 1, stream data: the stream number, then one Noise message of 1 to 65,535 bytes. Kind 2, a release piece: release.get's request id, then 1 to 262,144 bytes. Decoding `bytes` must give `frame`, and encoding `frame` must give `bytes`; or decoding must be refused with `expect`, checked in this order: truncated (no bytes at all), unknownKind (byte 0 not 1 or 2), truncated (fewer than 5 bytes), badLength (a payload of no bytes or over its kind's bound). `closes`: every close code of a hub link or a relay link, by `name` and `code`, and what the side whose link it closes does next (`reconnect`): backoff, reconnect on its back-off (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 s, then every 60 s); wait, wait the last `limit` frame's retryAfterMs or 10 minutes first (4001 replaced, 4426 no shared version, 4429 over a limit); never (4403 refused: the operator refused this key), stop reconnecting, report it once, and try again only after the configuration changes or the side restarts. A link that drops with no code is backoff.
